x-changes.title: Make child-run creation public for developer runtimes
x-changes.detail:
Proposed public runtime API for developers operating their own runtime. Create or ensure an idempotent child agent run linked to the authenticated parent and tool-call identity. Require scoped parent execution authority and permission in the target project; preserve retry identity and lineage. Public describes supported external-developer access, not unauthenticated access or permission to control arbitrary runs. The published snapshot currently classifies this operation as an internal runtime callback. Creates one child agent run for each parent run and tool call. Repeating the same request returns the existing child run. Later retries of the parent run reuse the task conversation.

If `idempotency_scope` is `durable_task`, the same durable task and tool call return the original child run across parent runs.

Research requests must satisfy both the aggregate candidate limits and the size limit for the complete serialized request. The size calculation includes source context and JSON escaping. If the complete request exceeds the limit, the API returns `413` with `research-envelope-too-large` before enqueueing the run. Keep the complete source payload, and do not retry the same input automatically.

x-changes.title: Expose child event-writer token exchange under Runtime
x-changes.detail: Used by the framework child-run token exchange and durable child execution path to obtain a child-scoped event-writing credential. Proposed public Runtime API for registered developer-owned runtimes; the published snapshot currently labels it internal. The inspected implementation requires the parent event-writer authority tied to veryfront-server, verifies a direct child relationship and project binding, and bounds the child credential lifetime by the parent credential. Generalize admitted runtime identities through explicit registration/authorization before claiming external-runtime support; preserve all scoping checks. Keep credentials out of model-visible tool inputs. The existing nested path expresses delegation from parent to child and does not need a speculative rename. Delegates an expiring event-writer credential from an authenticated parent runtime to its direct child run, scoped to the child run identity and project.

Token authority is limited to writing events for the target run; it does not grant arbitrary run control. Support registered developer-owned runtimes through explicit runtime authorization. get.x-current-description:
Lists a run’s events in `event_id` order. Each event includes its typed span envelope.

**Visibility:** Editors receive the full diagnostic payload. Viewers receive the sanitized public representation. Opaque provider replay blocks are always redacted.

**Pagination:** Each page contains the first events in the requested order, up to `limit`, that fit within 10 MiB of serialized data. If the first event exceeds that size, the page returns it alone. Use `page_info.next` to retrieve the next page.

**Filters:** All filters use AND. The `search`, `span_id`, and `turn_id` filters evaluate the payload and envelope visible to the caller. With `include_descendants=true`, the response interleaves events from descendant runs that you can read.

**Task and workflow runs without stored events:** The response is a snapshot derived from the run’s current state, not a stored log. Stored and derived events are never mixed in one run. Each derived event has a fixed `event_id`: `RUN_STARTED` = 1, `STEP_STARTED` = 2, `RUN_LOG_CAPTURED` = 3, `STEP_FINISHED` = 4, and the terminal `RUN_FINISHED` or `RUN_ERROR` = 5. An event that does not apply leaves its id unused, so a cursor stays valid as the run progresses. The started events appear once `started_at` is set, with `status: running` and `created_at` equal to `started_at`. The log and step-end events appear only when the run is terminal. The step end is always `STEP_FINISHED`, and its `status` reports `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`, so a failed or cancelled run has exactly one `RUN_ERROR`. A pending run has no events. A run cancelled before it started has only its terminal event. These ids replaced position-based ids once, at deploy: a cursor saved into a derived lifecycle before then should restart from the beginning of that run.

Use [`GET /runs/{run_id}/events/summary`](https://veryfront.com/docs/cloud/rest/api-reference/runs/summarize-run-events) to count the same events with the same filters. Responses are private and must not be cached (`no-store`).

get.x-current-description:
Counts events without returning their payloads. The response includes totals, error counts, first and last event IDs, timestamps, counts by event class and type, and a time histogram.

Event-type counts use canonical names, including normalized legacy names. Results are ordered by count descending, then by name. Timestamps use whole milliseconds.

**Histogram:** `buckets` accepts 1–500 slices and defaults to 60. Slices cover `[first_event_at, last_event_at + 1 ms)`, use half-open `[start, end)` boundaries, and differ in width by at most 1 ms. Each event belongs to one slice. A slice’s boundaries can be passed directly to the event-list endpoint.

The slice count cannot exceed the time span in milliseconds. A 10 ms span therefore has at most 10 slices. When no events match, `buckets` is empty.

Filtering by `search`, `span_id`, or `turn_id` checks each candidate event’s caller-visible payload and envelope. These queries scan candidate rows rather than using database-only aggregation.

write.description: Tokens written to the provider cache.

total.description: Sum of input, output, cache-read and cache-write tokens.

TokenUsage.description: Input excludes cache reads/writes; output includes reasoning. Total is input + output + cache.read + cache.write. Null means unknown, never zero.

Usage.description: Shared usage shape for a run, descendant aggregate, or evaluation; capture_status describes token capture coverage. Cost can remain unavailable independently.

RunArtifact.description: An immutable file reference authorized through the run’s project and conversation permissions.

input.description: Business input supplied when the run was created.

output.description: Final business output; null until successful finalization.

error.description: Failure details, present only when the run failed.

parent_run_id.description: Immediate parent run ID, present on child runs.

root_run_id.description: Top-level ancestor run ID, present on child runs.

updated_at.description: When the resource last changed, including usage updates.

started_at.description: When the first execution attempt started, omitted before execution.

finished_at.description: When the run completed, failed or was cancelled.

runtime.description: Resolved logical runtime selection; main_branch identifies the selected main-branch deployment, not a worker process.

timeout_seconds.description: Deadline for the whole run in seconds, measured from its first start and including retries.

retry_limit.description: Maximum retries after the first attempt; only retryable failures are retried.

attempt.description: Current or last execution attempt, starting at 1; absent before execution.

exit_code.description: Runtime process exit code, or null when no exit code was recorded.

duration_ms.description: Elapsed time from first start to finish, including waits and retries; null when not finished.

tool_error_count.description: Recorded failed tool invocations during this run.

logs.description: Captured runtime text logs, when available.

start_mode.description: Recorded execution start mode, when available.

control.description: Pending control requests and the current wait.

task_id.description: Orchestration task ID, distinct from the execution definition.

input_message_id.description: Conversation message that supplied the input.

usage.description: Usage when available; unknown measurements are null.

active.description: Descendants that are pending, running or waiting.

usage.description: Aggregate usage of every descendant, excluding this run.

descendants.description: Counts and usage across all descendant runs, excluding this run.

schema.description: JSON Schema captured for this run; object schemas and boolean schemas are supported.

sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the pinned schema.

RunCreationReceipt.description: Minimal admission receipt for a caller who cannot read the created run. No private fields are disclosed.

CreateRunResult.description: The full created run when readable by the caller; otherwise only its admission receipt. Replay uses the same caller visibility.

reason.description: `not_recorded`: the server never stored the submitting credential. `identity_removed`: the recorded identity was later revoked or deleted.

legacy_role.description: Role tag stored with the response. It is not an authenticated actor type.

actor.description: Authenticated principal that submitted the response, or `unavailable` for a historical response without authoritative provenance.

redacted_fields.description: Names of submitted secret fields omitted from values.

run_id.description: Run waiting for this input.

title.description: Question or decision shown to the responder.

fields.description: Fields the responder can fill in.

requested_responder_type.description: Required responder role; the authenticated actor identifies who actually responded.

response.description: Submitted response, or null before submission or after cancellation or expiry.

resolved_at.description: When the request was submitted, cancelled or expired.

tool_call_id.description: Tool invocation waiting for the response.
